name: Belchite old town (Pueblo Viejo)
story: During the Republican Zaragoza offensive the Army of the East under General Sebastián Pozas, with the XI and XV International Brigades, turned on Belchite when the drive on Zaragoza stalled. Thousands of soldiers and civilians were inside the town. Republican troops went in on 1 September and fought house by house, and the town fell on 6 September. Losses were heavy on both sides, and many defenders were taken prisoner. After the war Franco left the ruins as a monument and built a new Belchite next to them. The Trujal, once a Nationalist memorial inside the ruins, now honours all who died in the battle.
see: Shell-scarred churches of San Martín de Tours and San Agustín, the Torre del Reloj, the Arco de San Roque and streets of roofless houses. There is also the Trujal memorial.
plan: Entry is by guided tour only (about 1½ hours, starting at the Arco de la Villa). Day tours run every day; night tours on Friday and Saturday focus more on local legends than on the battle. Buy tickets at the tourist office (C/ Becú 2, new town) or on belchite.es, and check prices and times there just before you go.

vis.label: Booking
vis.text: Guided tour only; tickets at belchite.es or the tourist office, C/ Becú 2. Times and prices vary by season: check belchite.es

boxes.text: Casualty and prisoner totals for Belchite vary widely between sources, and depend on whether they count the town alone or the whole Zaragoza offensive, so this guide does not give a single figure.
